#en:
I used to mark my days by launch windows and grav-well tides. Now I count them by how long the comm stays quiet. Funny thing no one tells you about vanishing off the boards: silence is loud. Out here, with only the hum of the drive and my own notes on the console, the choices I made sound different. Not better, not worse. Just stripped of everyone else's speeches about duty and service and the greater good.

I keep thinking about Vallejos from the office in The Well. She used to bring in terrible TerraBrew, burn it half to slag, and still smile like we were saving the frontier one form at a time. We drifted apart before I ever touched a falsified route. Too busy, different shifts, then different postings. It was that easy to lose someone who thought the system would catch everyone if we just worked harder. I wonder what she would say now, seeing where those "proper channels" left Theta and the other ghosts.

People keep calling what I did criminal, like that word draws a clean line. As if rerouting one convoy around a pirate nest is noble, but rerouting another away from a slaughterhouse of a colony plan somehow crosses into sin. Truth is, we are all bargaining lives for trajectories; I just stopped pretending otherwise. When I nudged those manifests, when I bent the Silent Span to my own pattern, that was the first time I felt honest. No more hiding behind algorithms someone else wrote. No more shrugging and saying the regs did not allow an exception. I am the exception.

There was a tech on a border freighter who begged me to pass along an alternate corridor to his family ship. I had it. I could have sent it. Instead I watched him squirm, made him explain every risk twice, listened to the panic in his voice, and then told him to stick to the official lane. It did not feel like cruelty; it felt like clarity. If he could not see the sky the way I do, he had no business in the deep routes. I think about that moment more than I think about any pirate I burned with a bad interception vector.

I fled because the mask was slipping anyway. The LIST suits wanted clean numbers, clean reports. The UC wanted order. Freestar wanted plausible deniability. Everyone wants to believe they are different from the smugglers and pirates and zealots, but in the end they pull the same levers, just with cleaner gloves. I am done pretending. I am not better than the rest of them. I am simply not lying to myself about what it costs to carve a safe path through a hostile sky.

As for where I went, let them guess. They will follow the noise: the derelicts that are not as dead as they look, the homesteads with landing scars nobody logged, the comm buoys that blink wrong if you know how to read them. They will chase rumors of Horizon's Fold like it is a prize. Maybe they will even get close. But the real me lives between the charts now, in the margins of routes I have already rewritten. Whoever finally closes the distance will discover that a navigator's last sanctuary is not a place. It is the fact that every path they took to reach me was mine long before it was theirs.
zh:
我以前用发射窗口和重力井潮汐来标记我的日子。如今我按通讯安静了多久来数。关于从名单上消失，没人告诉你的一件有趣事是：沉默很响。在这外面，只有驱动的嗡鸣和我自己在控制台上的笔记，我做过的选择听起来不一样了。不是更好，不是更糟。只是被剥去了别人关于职责、服务和更大利益的说辞。

我总想起深井区办公室里那个瓦列霍斯。她常带来难喝的地球酿酒，把它烧成半渣，还笑得像我们在一次一份表格地拯救边疆。在我碰过任何伪造航线之前我们就疏远了。太忙、班次不同、然后调去不同岗位。失去一个以为只要我们更努力系统就会接住所有人的人，就那么容易。我想知道她如今会说什么，看着那些"正规渠道"把忒塔和其他鬼留在了哪里。

人们不断把我做的事叫犯罪，像那个词能画出干净的界线。仿佛把一支运输队绕开海盗巢穴是高尚的，把另一支绕开一个屠宰场般的殖民地计划却不知怎的就越界成了罪。事实是，我们都在拿性命换轨迹；我只是停止假装不是这样。当我拨动那些清单、当我把静默跨距弯成我自己的图案时，那是我第一次感到诚实。不再躲在别人写的算法后面。不再耸肩说规章不允许例外。我就是那个例外。

有一艘边境货船上有个技工，求我把一条备选走廊转给他的家用船。我有它。我本可以发出去。可我看着他扭动，逼他把每一处风险都解释两遍，听着他声音里的惊慌，然后叫他老实走官方航道。它不感觉像残忍；它感觉像清明。要是他不能像我这样看天空，他就没资格走深航道。我想到那个瞬间，比我想到任何我用糟糕拦截矢量烧掉的海盗都多。

我逃走，是因为面具反正也快掉了。独立盟的西装们要干净的数字、干净的报告。联殖要秩序。自由星系联盟要可推诿。每个人都想相信自己与走私贩、海盗和狂信徒不同，可到头来他们拉的是同样的杆，只是手套更干净。我不再假装了。我并不比他们其余人好。我只是不再对自己撒谎，说在敌意的天空中凿出一条安全的路要付出什么代价。

至于我去了哪里，让他们猜。他们会追着噪声走：那些没那么死的弃船、那些带着没人记录过着陆痕的农家院、那些只要你会读就眨得不对的通讯浮标。他们会把"地平线的褶皱"的传言当战利品一样追。也许他们甚至会靠近。可真正的我如今活在星图之间，在我已经改写过的航线的页边。最终缩短距离的人会发现，一个领航员最后的避难所不是一个地方。而是一个事实：他们到达我这里的每一条路，早在我把它变成他们的路之前，就已经是我的了。

#en:
When I was little on that cramped station outside Sol, I used to think space was a clean slate. No history, no lies, just stars and the straight line between two points. I wanted to build ships that never broke and systems that never failed, like some kid drawing perfect circles in a notebook and believing the pencil would never dull. It is almost funny now, how certain I was that clever design could fix what people are.

I keep telling myself I did not flee. I "repositioned assets," "mitigated risk," "exercised unilateral discretion in the absence of trustworthy governance." Wrap it in enough precision and it sounds like policy instead of panic. The truth sits there underneath, ugly and simple I tampered with minds and systems I was supposed to protect, and when the light swung my way I ran.

This place made sense because it is a junction, a place where signals cross more often than people look up. I have always liked those. Neon, Gagarin, the underbelly clinics, that drifting hauler pretending to be a hospital they all blur the line between official and not, and nobody asks where a data stream really came from as long as it does not trip an alarm. I need that noise around me now. It gives me interfaces to touch and excuses to reroute guilt into abstract packet flows and checksum failures.

I spend hours arguing with myself in systems language. I tell my conscience that I did not "erase" anyone, I reduced harmful loops, trimmed redundancies, optimized resilience under load. I insist that memory is just another dataset, that pruning it is a kindness, that entanglement with trauma is mathematically inefficient. I use words like entropic drift and cognitive overhead as if enough jargon will smother the sound of people screaming when they realize they have lost something they cannot name.

When the doubt claws through anyway, I bury it under models. Graphs of how many lives might be spared if certain officers forget certain orders, how many debtors in Gagarin will never see a collector because an account quietly ceases to exist. If I had not done it, someone worse would have taken the same tools and used them without even pretending to care. That is the line I feed myself at three in the morning while my fingers tap out key lengths on the table.

The frightening part is the moments I catch myself leaning forward, imagining the next escalation. Not just editing ledgers and battle logs, but whole identities, beliefs. What would it take to turn a zealot or a governor with a few carefully placed gaps and anchors, to see if the human mind can be rebuilt cleaner from inside out? For a second, the thought tastes sweet, like proof that all of this damage might be leading somewhere clever.

Then I remember that girl on the station, staring at the stars and thinking they were honest. I wish I could tell her that the sky is a liar and the only thing you can trust is the code you write yourself. I also wish she did not sound so disappointed in me when she walks through my dreams and refuses to forget what I have done, no matter how many times I try to rewrite it.
zh:
我小时候在太阳系外那座逼仄的空间站上，以为太空是一块干净的画板。没有历史，没有谎言，只有群星和两点之间的直线。我想造永不损坏的飞船和不失效的系统，像某个小孩在笔记本上画完美的圆、相信铅笔永远不会钝。现在几乎有点好笑，我当年那么确信聪明的设计能修好人的本性。

我一直告诉自己我没有逃。我"重新配置了资产""缓解了风险""在缺乏可信治理的情况下行使了单方面裁量权"。用足够的精确把它包起来，它听起来就像政策而不是惊慌。真相在底下摆着，丑陋而简单——我篡改了我本该保护的心智和系统，而当光照到我身上时，我跑了。

这地方说得通，因为它是个交汇点，一个信号穿过得比人们抬头看更频繁的地方。我一向喜欢这种地方。霓虹城、加加林、下层诊所、那艘假装是医院的漂流货船——它们都模糊了官方与非官方的界线，而只要不触发警报，没人问一条数据流究竟来自哪里。我现在需要周围那种噪声。它给我可以去碰的接口，和把愧疚改道成抽象数据包流与校验和失败的借口。

我花好几个小时用系统语言跟自己争论。我告诉我的良心，我没有"抹除"任何人，我减少了有害循环、修剪了冗余、优化了负载下的韧性。我坚持记忆只是另一个数据集，修剪它是一种仁慈，与创伤的纠缠在数学上是低效的。我用"熵漂移"和"认知开销"这类词，像足够多的术语就能闷死人们意识到自己失去了某个叫不出名字的东西时尖叫的声音。

当怀疑还是扒进来时，我把它埋在模型底下。关于若某些军官忘掉某些命令能省下多少条命的图表，关于加加林多少个欠债人永远见不到讨债人，因为某个账户悄悄消失了。要是我没做，更糟的人会拿走同样的工具、用它们，甚至不假装在乎。这就是我凌晨三点用手指在桌上敲出密钥长度时喂给自己的说法。

可怕的是那些我发觉自己前倾、想象下一次升级的时刻。不只是编辑账簿和战斗日志，而是整个身份、信念。要花多大功夫才能把一个狂信徒或一个总督，用几个精心放置的缺口和锚点改造过来，看看人脑能否从里到外重造得更干净？有那么一瞬，那个念头尝起来是甜的，像证明所有这些伤害也许正引向某个聪明的地方。

然后我想起那座空间站上那个女孩，盯着星星、以为它们是诚实的。我希望我能告诉她，天空是个骗子，你唯一能信任的是你自己写的代码。我也希望她走过我梦里时不要对我显得那么失望，不要拒绝忘掉我做过的事，无论我试图改写它多少次。

#en:
I am writing this in the dark between pulses. The relay is on minimum power, just enough to keep the diagnostics awake and the dishes twitching like they still belong to the UC. It is a good place to disappear; everyone thinks this node is dead, an accounting error left in orbit. The smugglers using its shadow have no idea what the boards are really listening for. They only care that their cargo gets through. I care about the numbers.

Sometimes I remember the woman on Jemison who argued in conference rooms and believed anyone in the MAST tower could be persuaded by clean simulations. She turned up with sleep in her eyes and a stack of anomaly reports, begged politely for someone to look. I know her face from old ID photos and bathroom mirrors. All I feel for her now is contempt. She thought the system cared about being right. I have enough data now to prove it only cares about not being blamed.

People like to call what I am doing selfish. They mean it as an accusation, but it is just an imprecise word for self-preservation with better math. If a corporation can write off a convoy and sleep at night, why should I treat my own survival as anything less than a priority variable The rational approach is to assume that no one will protect you unless your disappearance costs them more than your existence. So I adjust the equations. I make sure the worst actors occasionally experience the risks they externalize. And I carve out enough leverage that when someone finally does come looking, there is a real price attached to laying hands on me.

I chose this relay because it is a hinge in the network. Old UC infrastructure, forgotten, then "quietly reactivated" for reasons no one will put on paper. From here I can push corrections into lanes that were never updated to modern standards; any failures get blamed on aging hardware and underfunded maintenance. The Silk Collective do not ask why their routes suddenly became more efficient. They pass along rumors from captains who felt their drives "catch" at the last second, like someone unseen tapped the hull and moved them out of the way. They speak of it softly, over drinks, like a superstition. In those same lanes, other ships do not come back.

I am afraid, of course. Not of dying. Of being erased. Of my work being swept into the same oubliette where they put the convoy report and the analyst's missing folders. That is why I leave echoes data caches hidden in places no one checks, old colleagues nudged into noticing patterns they will not be able to unsee. Someone is following the trail already. The timing offsets I used to consider my private signature are starting to come back to me in intercepted chatter.

So I will stay at this node until one of two curves crosses the line the risk of remaining exceeds the utility of what I can still do from here, or the hunter behind me proves they can read the sky as well as I can. Then I move to the next quiet place on the network and adjust the vectors again. The lanes are not safe and pretending otherwise is the first lie they teach you. I am just making that lie harder to sustain.
zh:
我在脉冲之间的黑暗里写下这些。中继站开到最低功率，刚好够让诊断程序醒着、让天线像仍属于联殖那样抽动着。这是个消失的好地方；所有人都以为这个节点死了，一处留在轨道上的记账错误。利用它阴影的走私贩们完全不知道那些主板真正在听什么。他们只在乎自己的货能通过。我在乎数字。

有时我记起杰米森那个在会议室里争论、相信联殖塔里任何人都能被干净的模拟说服的女人。她带着睡意和一摞异常报告出现，礼貌地恳求有人看一眼。我从旧证件照和浴室镜子里认得她的脸。如今我对她只有轻蔑。她以为这套系统在乎对不对。我现在有足够的数据证明它只在乎不被怪罪。

人们喜欢把我做的事叫自私。他们说这话是指控，但那只是一个不精确的词，指用更好的数学进行的自保。要是一家企业能勾销一支运输队还睡得着，我为什么该把自己的生存看得低于一个优先变量？理性的做法是假设：除非你的消失让他们付出的代价高于你的存在，否则没人会保护你。所以我调整方程。我确保最坏的行为者偶尔尝到他们外部化的那些风险。我凿出足够的筹码，好让最终真有人来查时，把手放在我身上会附带真实的代价。

我选这座中继站，因为它是网络里的一个铰链。旧联殖基础设施，被遗忘，然后因为没人愿意写进纸面的原因"被悄悄重新激活"。从这里，我能把修正推入那些从未升级到现代标准的航道；任何故障都被怪到老化的硬件和经费不足的维护上。丝绸集体不问他们的航线为什么突然变得更高效。他们传递着船长们的传言——那些人感到自己的驱动在最后一秒"卡"了一下，像某个看不见的人拍了拍船壳、把他们挪开。他们低声谈着，就着酒，像在说一种迷信。在同样的航道里，别的飞船回不来。

我当然害怕。不是怕死。是怕被抹除。怕我的作品被扫进他们放置运输队报告和分析师失踪文件夹的同一间遗忘地牢。这就是为什么我留下回声——藏在没人检查之处的数据缓存、被轻推着注意到些他们无法再当没看见的图案的老同事。已经有人在顺着痕迹追了。那些曾被我视作私人签名的时序偏移，开始以截获的闲聊的形式回到我这里。

所以我会留在这个节点，直到两条曲线中的一条越过那条线——留下继续的风险超过我还能从这里做成的事的价值，或者我身后的猎人证明他能像我一样读天空。然后我移到网络上下一个安静的地方，再次调整矢量。航道不安全，假装它安全是他们教你的第一个谎言。我只是让那个谎言更难维持。

#en:
Mara says I grind my teeth in my sleep again. Keira says that is rich, coming from someone who hums reactor warning tones when she is nervous. Maybe they are both right. Hard to come back from a day like today and just switch off. The suit is still outgassing in the locker and I swear I can smell scorched polymer and old coolant through the bulkhead.

We swung out to that freighter wreck sitting just off the lane, the one people keep calling the Widowlight. Nullspace grabbed the contract before the yard-rats even finished whispering the ghost stories about it. Mara was on point, cutting the approach hatch; Keira floated rear guard, coil-clip running like always, jaw set behind her visor. I went mid, charge kit on my hip, listening to the crunch of our mag-boots and the dull echoes in a hull that should have been busier in its last minutes than the logs claim.

Inside, it was the usual chaos frozen mid-breath. Loose cargo, a half-collapsed stanchion, a flight chair still strapped with no one in it. No bodies, though. I would rather pick my way through bones than emptiness. At least bones mean you can stop asking where everybody went. Mara chattered on crew channel to keep things light, but she went quiet when we hit the forward storage bay and saw those sealed drums lined up too neat, labels scrubbed, registry tags half-melted instead of popped clean. Burn-scars around the data ports. Someone wanted whatever had been in there to vanish from record, not just from space.

We called in the find like we are supposed to, but not before Keira slipped me a look and killed her mic for two heartbeats. That is our whole life in a glance: what do we tell them, what do we keep, and what will come back around to kill us if we are greedy or stupid. In the old days, back when Nullspace was still carving out a name, we would have cracked one drum and taken our chances. Now other crews nod when Damon Harker and the Nullspace patch walk into a bar, and that feels like a weight as much as a win. Recognition buys better contracts, sure, but it also means people notice when you come back from a ghost-ship with more than you should.

On the way out I caught myself thinking about that survey run we picked clean last cycle, the one where the beacon logs did not match the debris pattern and there was talk of a missing crew that never filed distress. Same hollow quiet, same feeling of walking through someone else's unfinished argument. I keep telling myself it is just bad routing and worse luck, that not every empty deck is part of some bigger pattern. But I saw the way Mara's eyes tracked those dead drums, and I saw Keira flinch when the nav plotted our exit vector right along a lane that has had more "accidents" than it should.

Pride keeps me signing on the dotted line, keeps me strapping in when Nullspace gets called first instead of last. Fear keeps my tether double-checked and a hand near the cutter trigger. Between those two, there is just enough room left to wonder if one day we will be the story the next salvage crew tells themselves not to think about as they step through our broken airlock.
zh:
玛拉说我睡觉时又磨牙了。基娅说这话从一个紧张时哼反应堆警报音的人嘴里说出来可真够呛。也许她们俩都说对了。像今天这样的一天过后，很难回来就关掉。宇航服还在储物柜里排气，我发誓我能透过舱壁闻到烧焦的聚合物和旧冷却液。

我们绕到那艘就停在航道外的货船残骸，那艘人们一直叫它"寡妇灯"的。空域在船坞老鼠们还没低声讲完关于它的鬼故事之前就拿下了合同。玛拉打头，切割进近舱门；基娅殿后飘着，线圈夹像往常一样运转，下巴在面罩后绷紧。我在中间，髋上挂着炸药包，听着我们磁靴的碾压声和船壳里沉闷的回响——那船壳在它生命的最后几分钟本该比日志所称的更忙。

里面是寻常的、凝在呼吸中途的混乱。散落的货物、半塌的支柱、一张系着安全带却空无一人的驾驶椅。不过没有尸体。比起空荡，我宁愿在骸骨间穿行。至少骸骨意味着你可以停止追问人去哪了。玛拉在船员频道上闲聊想让大家放松，可当我们走到前部储藏舱、看见那些密封桶排得太整齐、标签被擦掉、登记标签半熔而不是干净脱落时，她安静了。数据端口周围有烧痕。有人想让那里面的东西从记录里消失，而不只是从太空里消失。

我们按该做的上报了发现，但在此之前基娅递给我一个眼神，把话筒掐灭了两拍心跳。那就是我们整个生活浓缩在一个眼神里：我们告诉他们什么，我们留下什么，以及要是我们贪或蠢，什么会回来要我们的命。早年，空域还在打名气的时候，我们会撬开一只桶赌一把。如今别的船员看到达蒙·哈克和空域的标志走进酒吧会点头，而那既像是一种胜利，也像一份重量。被认出来确实能换来更好的合同，但也意味着当你带着不该有的东西从一艘鬼船上回来时，人们会注意到。

出来的路上，我发觉自己在想上个周期我们清空的那次勘测——那次的信标日志与碎片图案对不上，还有关于一队从未发出求救的失踪船员的议论。同样空洞的安静，同样走在别人未完成争论里的感觉。我一直告诉自己那只是糟糕的航路和更糟的运气，不是每一条空荡的甲板都属于某个更大的图案。可我看见玛拉的眼睛如何追踪那些死桶，看见基娅在导航把我们的撤离矢量画在一条"事故"多得异常的航道上时如何畏缩。

骄傲让我在虚线上签字，让空域被第一个而不是最后一个叫到时我系好安全带。恐惧让我的系绳被检查两遍、一只手靠近切割机扳机。在这两者之间，只剩刚够的空间去琢磨：有一天我们会不会成为下一支打捞队在跨过我们破开的气闸时告诉自己别去想的那个故事。
